```python
# [file: examples/browser/parallel_browser.py]
async def main():
    # Create 3 separate browser instances
    browsers = [
        Browser(
            user_data_dir=f'./temp-profile-{i}',
            headless=False,
        )
        for i in range(3)
    ]

    # Create 3 agents with different tasks
    agents = [
        Agent(
            task='Search for "browser automation" on Google',
            browser=browsers[0],
            llm=ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4.1-mini'),
        ),
        Agent(
            task='Search for "AI agents" on DuckDuckGo',
            browser=browsers[1],
            llm=ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4.1-mini'),
        ),
        Agent(
            task='Visit Wikipedia and search for "web scraping"',
            browser=browsers[2],
            llm=ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4.1-mini'),
        ),
    ]

    # Run all agents in parallel
    tasks = [agent.run() for agent in agents]
    results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)

    print('🎉 All agents completed!')
```

```python
browser = Browser(

)
```

```python
# [file: examples/custom-functions/parallel_agents.py]
async def run_single_agent(task: str, llm, agent_id: int) -> tuple[int, str]:
    import tempfile
    from browser_use.browser import BrowserSession
    from browser_use.browser.profile import BrowserProfile

    temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=f'browser_agent_{agent_id}_')

    profile = BrowserProfile()
    profile.user_data_dir = temp_dir
    profile.headless = False
    profile.keep_alive = False

    profile.args = [
        '--disable-popup-blocking',
        '--disable-extensions',
        '--disable-plugins',
        '--disable-images',
        '--no-first-run',
        '--disable-default-apps',
        '--disable-background-timer-throttling',
        '--disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows',
        '--disable-renderer-backgrounding',
    ]

    browser_session = BrowserSession(browser_profile=profile)

    await browser_session.start()
    # ...
    agent = Agent(task=task, llm=llm, browser_session=browser_session, preload=False)
    result = await asyncio.wait_for(agent.run(), timeout=300)
    # ...
    await browser_session.kill()
```

## 2. One local Chrome instance reused, one agent at a time

If you specifically want *the same* local Chrome profile (for shared logins, cookies, etc.) and are okay with serial execution per browser, you can do:

```python

    executable_path='/path/to/your/chrome',
    user_data_dir='~/path/to/your/profile',
    profile_directory='Default',

)
```

This is just the **Real Browser** pattern from `AGENTS.md` (section “Real Browser”) where one `Browser` is connected to an existing Chrome instance and given to an `Agent`.

Running multiple agents truly *concurrently* on the same physical Chrome profile is generally not supported well (one browser process, one controlling agent at a time), so the examples focus on either:

- several **independent** Chrome-based sessions (parallel), or

I found the solution on my own. Maybe it will be useful to someone. 

You can run as many local Google Chrome instances as you like with this command:
```
google-chrome --remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir=/tmp/chrome-1 &
```

Changing the port and profile directory each time. 

And then you can run multiple agents in parallel like this with different ports: 
```
config = BrowserConfig(
  cdp_url="http://localhost:9222"
) 
```

This works because Browser Use supports connecting to an existing browser via Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) using the `cdp_url` parameter. By specifying different `cdp_url` values (e.g., `http://localhost:9222`, `http://localhost:9223`, etc.), you can connect multiple agents to separate Chrome instances running on different debugging ports.
